players.product: AI / HPC data-center campuses on owned powered land (Hannibal campus with pending Long Ridge, Matagorda County TX; developed with Starwood) plus Exaion sovereign private cloud for AI inference in Europe

quarterly_data.signal: MARA 10-K: 2025 bitcoin mining revenue was $872,401 thousand versus $599,436 thousand in 2024; other digital assets mining revenue was $11,584 thousand versus $23,025 thousand, hosting services $4,668 thousand versus $31,638 thousand and other revenue $18,440 thousand versus $2,279 thousand. MARA produced 8,799 BTC in 2025 versus 9,430 in 2024 (average 24.1 BTC per day versus 25.8) at an average price of BTC mined of $101,221 versus $66,249; it won 2,588 blocks versus 2,132, and transaction fees were 1.1% of the total versus 6.2%.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 bitcoin mining revenue $872,401 thousand; 8,799 BTC produced; 2,588 blocks won

quarterly_data.signal: MARA 10-K revenue disaggregation for arrangements in which MARA is the Operator and Participant (mining): 2025 mining operator block rewards were $829,949 thousand versus $557,575 thousand in 2024, mining operator transaction fees $9,205 thousand versus $32,884 thousand, and mining participant revenue $44,831 thousand versus $32,002 thousand.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 operator block rewards $829,949 thousand; operator transaction fees $9,205 thousand; participant $44,831 thousand

quarterly_data.signal: MARA 10-K fleet: energized hashrate was 66.4 EH/s at December 31, 2025 versus 53.2 EH/s a year earlier (24.7 EH/s at end-2023), with miner efficiency of 18.6 joules per terahash versus 19.2 (25.0 at end-2023). Owned sites held 37.2 EH/s of energized hashrate (Central Texas 21.8, East Ohio 4.0, North Texas 2.4, Central Ohio 1.3, Central Nebraska 5.5, International 2.3) and hosted sites 29.2 EH/s (Central North Dakota 16.6, West Texas 10.2, Other 2.4).

MARA 10-K: 2025 third-party hosting and other energy costs were $292,243 thousand versus $257,276 thousand in 2024, and purchased energy costs $179,041 thousand versus $98,160 thousand. MARA contracts with various service providers for hosting, operational support and construction of data centers where its equipment is deployed; these contracts typically require prepayments to the service providers, classified as Deposits and Long-term deposits.
